newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ex-WTO chief optimistic about China entry in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ex-WTO chief optimistic about China entry in 1998.

text.p: China could join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in 1998 if the key players maintain a strong political commitment to the goal, Peter Sutherland, the WTO's first director general, said on Monday.

Sutherland, now chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs International, told a luncheon that China's goal of completing talks by the end of this year is realistic, "but only if a powerful political will on all sides is maintained".

If the negotiations can be completed in good time, China could join the group in 1998, the 50th anniversary of a world trade regime begun with the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and succeeded by the WTO.

Sutherland said China has made several key concessions, including promises to implement full trading rights for all enterprises within three years of joining the WTO and to accept the WTO's standards on intellectual property rights upon joining.
"One has to recognise that China has made real progress in making a positive move forward," he said.
But issues relating to tariff and non-tariff barriers as well as China's opening of trade in agricultural products and services still must be addressed, Sutherland said.

"But beyond what has or has not been accomplished in the last few months, the important development is that you can now sense on both sides of the talks, particularly between China and the U.S., a strong political commitment to make the negotiations succeed," he said.

Sutherland said a strong political commitment is necessary to fight U.S. protectionist forces as well as opponents trying to block China's inclusion in the WTO on grounds that the country's leaders fail to honour human rights.
Despite these roadblocks, Sutherland said he expects the White House to support China's joining.
"The U.S. always has delivered on free trade," he said, citing the North American Free Trade Pact (NAFTA) and the Uruguay Round of GATT pacts.
